question: Can an agent learn how strongly to trust measured predictions on difficult rows using training feedback, above the previously elected equal average?
design: Reuse the three 4061-row frozen models and their already sealed probabilities. Learn one small regularized correction on 808 separate training rows, then apply it without changes to the 817 and 807 later rows. These panels have previously served a screening experiment and remain development evidence.
model: Use a fixed equal-probability incumbent from nomination. Fit one penalized logistic correction with that incumbent's log-odds as an offset. Only use odds differences, disagreement and confidence from the three anonymous prediction columns. Use a convex squared penalty centered on zero and fix inverse strength in advance at 1/16. Shrinkage preserves the incumbent when support for a correction is weak. No per-dataset or per-row rules and no calibrated threshold changes after scoring.
gate: Predeclare two comparisons to report, corrected versus the screened equal mix and corrected versus the original tree. Require a nonnegative net number correct in both later panels and a pooled increase of at least 0.30 percentage points over the equal mix to advance. A successful result warrants fresh grouped testing before integration. The same screened results cannot qualify a new release. No course validation or test.
